exercises.text: There are 5 red balls, 6 white balls, 8 blue balls and 6 green balls in the drawing drum. We will randomly select three balls. What is the probability that we will get the following sequence of the balls: a) white, blue, red, b) green, red, green, c) white, white, white, d) red, blue, green? First, consider (A) sampling without replacement, and then (B) sampling with replacement.

parts.q: (A) without replacement · a) white, blue, red
(A) without replacement · b) green, red, green
(A) without replacement · c) white, white, white
(A) without replacement · d) red, blue, green
(B) with replacement · a) white, blue, red
(B) with replacement · b) green, red, green

exercises.text: Random variable X expresses the lifespan of lightbulbs in hours. Interpret the value of 1% quantile (x0.01).

parts.model: x0.01 is the lifespan (in hours) that only 1 % of lightbulbs do not exceed: P(X ≤ x0.01) = 0.01. So 1 % of bulbs fail within x0.01 hours and 99 % last longer.
